text:
alex: FYI customer ACME reporting sustained 502/504s to hosted API since ~02:10 UTC, started right after billing-cache eviction job. ticket #4321. sample curl and x-request-id below. can we triage?

maria: assigning, thanks. can you paste a request id and a short repro? @jon can you watch logs for upstream 502/504s? :eyes:

alex: request ids: x-request-id=acme-req-8f3a, trace=trace-02f. repro curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "x-request-id: acme-req-8f3a" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

jon: looking at edge logs (envoy/nginx). seeing lots of upstream reset and 504s hitting frontdoor and auth proxy. excerpt:
```
[02:12:14] envoy upstream reset: STREAM_RESET (reason=FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR) x-request-id=acme-req-8f3a upstream=auth-proxy-02
[02:12:15] nginx 502 "upstream prematurely closed connection" x-request-id=acme-req-8f3a
[02:12:16] proxy 504 read timeout waiting for upstream response (upstream=hosted-model-1)
```
jon: trend shows auth-proxy CPU spike and connection pool exhaustion around 02:09-02:13.

maria: hypothesis — billing-cache eviction caused a storm of billing lookups which pushed auth-proxy to thrash K/V lookups and hit h2 keepalive pools. edge then returned 502/504 as upstreams refused streams. any traces from billing or redis?

leo: pulled billing service metrics: huge fanout after eviction job (cache-miss blast). redis latency jumped to 1500ms at peak, causing auth calls to block. also saw auth-service error 429s.

alex: customer reported timeouts for batch embeddings and normal generate endpoints, symptomatic of upstream slowdowns. they sent a stacktrace from client showing repeated retries -> 502.

jon: repro steps to simulate locally: 1) flush billing cache; 2) run a tight loop `for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H "x-request-id: test-$i" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done` 3) watch `kubectl logs -f deploy/auth-proxy` — you'll see connection pool errors and `http2: stream closed` logs.

maria: mitigation plan: immediate - revert eviction (repopulate TTL) and increase auth-proxy h2 connection pool and auth cache TTL; short-term - add request queuing/backpressure on billing lookups; follow-up - circuit-break billing calls and add burst smoothing job.

leo: I pushed a stop to the eviction job at 02:18 UTC and patched billing to warm a subset of keys. also applied a temporary increase to auth-proxy env var `H2_MAX_STREAMS=200` and bumped cache TTL to 30m.

sre-bot: deploy started: rollout auth-proxy replicas=+2 at 02:20 UTC (job id r-8842).

jon: after changes, error rate dropped ~93% by 02:26 UTC, latency back to baseline by 02:30. sampling the same curl now returns 200s. `x-request-id=acme-req-8f3a` trace shows successful path.

alex: reported back to customer; they confirmed restores service for their workload. will keep the ticket open until we complete follow-up items. :thumbsup:

maria: follow-ups created: ENG-972 (billing eviction smoothing), ENG-973 (auth-proxy pool/circuit-breakers), ENG-974 (runbook for eviction jobs). tagging oncall to review circuit-break thresholds.

leo: notes for postmortem: avoid simultaneous full-cache evictions across regions; add progressive warmup, rate-limited refill, and monitoring alert for redis p95 > 200ms causing auth thrash.

jon: quick pointer logs/trace ids to attach for postmortem: acme-req-8f3a, trace-02f, deploy r-8842.

maria: thanks team. closing triage, will draft summary and link the follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
